# The conference year, stage by stage

The conference pages are built to go up before all the details are known.
Everything that changes during the year lives in the **AP-LS Conference**
Google Sheet, so most updates never touch the website files at all.

The update loop is always the same:

1. Edit the Sheet.
2. Run `source("conferences/_update-conference.R")` from the project root.
3. Render the conference pages and check them in the browser.

## The five stages

| Stage | When | What you do |
| ----- | ---- | ----------- |
| 1 | Conference announced | Done at the yearly setup: city, dates, hotel, and photos are already on the page. |
| 2 | Call for proposals opens | Set the CFP keys in the `info` tab, then follow the STAGE 2 comment in `cfp/index.qmd` to make the full call visible. |
| 3 | Room block opens | Set `hotel_note` and `hotel_booking_url` in the `info` tab. The booking callout appears on its own. |
| 4 | Schedule released | Set `schedule_note` in the `info` tab. |
| 5 | Registration opens | Set `registration_note` and `registration_url`, and put the final prices in the rates tabs. The Register button appears on its own. |

## What the Sheet controls

- The announcement note in each section of the main page
- The CFP announcement, deadline, portal link, and reviewer form link
- The room-block note and booking link (and whether the callout shows)
- The registration note and link (and whether the Register button shows)
- Registration and workshop rates tables
- The workshop pages themselves, one row per workshop

## What still lives in the page files

The yearly facts (year, city, dates, hotel name and address), the photos,
the section headings, and the full text of the call for proposals. Those
change once a year at most, and the yearly setup chapter covers them.

The pages read local copies of the Sheet data, committed alongside the
site. Visitors always see the last rendered version, and the site builds
fine even when Google Drive is unreachable.
